S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder is defined by a persistent preoccupation with one or more perceived defects in appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors or mental acts such as checking, comparing, grooming, or reassurance seeking. It often has a chronic or fluctuating course and becomes clinically significant when the appearance concern causes distress or functional impairment. It is distinguished from ordinary appearance dissatisfaction by the intensity, repetitiveness, and impairment, and from eating-disorder presentations when the concern is not primarily about weight or body fat.

patient.stressor_event: Foreclosure on a mortgage or loan
patient.stressor: When crop losses and delayed grant funding led to foreclosure proceedings on a farm loan, Lawson had to meet more often with bankers, county officials, and potential donors for the agro-art retreat he had dreamed about. During that period, his longstanding worry narrowed onto a perceived roughness and aged look in his face and hands, flaws that his wife and younger farm workers saw as ordinary signs of outdoor labor. Over an unclear span, he began losing work time to repeated checking, hat adjustments, and mental comparisons before meetings or community events, and he increasingly avoided being photographed for grant materials or craft-fair publicity. He entered psychiatric care after his primary-care physician noticed that the appearance concern was interfering with farm decisions and referred him to a psychiatrist.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: What brings me in is that I can't get past how rough and worn my face and hands look, like every banker or county person is staring at the cracks, spots, and sagging even though my wife says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before I leave for a loan meeting or a craft-fair table, I keep checking the truck mirror and bathroom mirror, turning my hat this way and that and comparing my hands to the younger workers' until I've wasted time I should be using on the farm.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I've missed calls with bankers and put off farm decisions because I couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to sit down with people, and I've stopped agreeing to photos that would help promote the retreat and craft sales.
